passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Gary Lemons passed a polygraph examination that confirmed his statements to investigators about Bowman.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Both Bowman and Lemons appeared before the grand jury. Details of their testimony were not released.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Virginia Adopts Statewide AMBER Alert Following Jennifer Short’s Abduction: Approximately three months after 9-year-old Jennifer Short disappeared from her Henry County home, Virginia adopted a statewide AMBER Alert plan designed to rapidly distribute information about abducted children.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The Roanoke Times specifically reported that the program was adopted after Jennifer’s disappearance and other similar tragedies.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Under the new system, Virginia State Police would operate the AMBER Alert Plan and coordinate efforts statewide.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: When activated, police could quickly distribute information through radio and television broadcasts.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The Virginia Department of Transportation would electronically alert motorists through highway information signs and notify other police departments.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The program was intended to replace the slower process of individually contacting numerous agencies and media outlets when a child disappeared.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Virginia State Police spokeswoman Ellen Qualls said the system was designed to get information out quickly and efficiently across the state.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Henry County Sheriff’s Capt. Kimmy Nester said the idea for such a statewide system was “quick-response programs such as the Amber Alert” and supported having a coordinated statewide approach.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Before the statewide program was established, local governments, including Roanoke, already had local AMBER Alert programs.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The article reported that plans were also underway for a statewide AMBER Alert system in North Carolina, where Jennifer’s remains had been recovered.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The Shorts’ home and belongings were sold at auction, with proceeds going to the family estate.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Forensic testing of some items collected from Bowman’s residences in North Carolina and Canada was negative.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The reward stood at $42,000, after some donors withdrew contributions following the discovery of Jennifer’s remains.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators said they still wanted to interview many people, not just Garrison Bowman.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Henry County Sheriff Frank Cassell said Bowman was a person of interest, but emphasized that investigators were also interested in other individuals, including people in Henry County.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman’s attorney, William Cleveland, said Bowman had been interviewed several times and investigators had already searched his possessions, including a van, while he was in Canada.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Bowman had passed a Virginia State Police polygraph in which he denied involvement in the murders.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: According to the article, investigators said they had found no evidence tying Bowman to the Short murders at that point.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: A special grand jury in Charlottesville investigated the Short case. The newspaper specifically states this was not a continuation of the Bowman grand jury.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators again searched the Rockingham County area where Jennifer’s remains had been discovered.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: The Roanoke forensic laboratory received assistance to accelerate testing in the Short investigation.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Jennifer would have turned 10.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Authorities diverted or dammed the creek so investigators could search areas that had previously been underwater.

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Henry County Sheriff H.F. “Frank” Cassell said investigators recovered several “articles” during the search but declined to identify the items because the triple-homicide investigation remained active

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Investigators did not publicly disclose whether the recovered items were ultimately determined to be connected to Jennifer or her murder

passages.section: Short Family Murder and Abduction Timeline
passages.text: Search of Jennifer’s Recovery Site: Investigators returned to the area in Rockingham County, North Carolina, where Jennifer Short’s remains had been discovered and conducted an intensive search for additional evidence.
